Quick technical summary from infra: we traced the spike to a combination of batching policy regression + an interaction with prefix KV-cache eviction that created a "resonance" effect (internal term). Sequence:

1) An unlucky batch boundary aligned with a set of long-horizon requests from Acme (large payloads).
2) The new adaptive batching change mis-sized several batches which increased head-of-line blocking on some inference workers.
3) Those workers started dropping prefix cache entries under memory pressure; prefix eviction policy then caused a burst of cache misses for similar prefixes (high locality for checkout templates).
4) Cache misses increase per-request latency -> client SDK retries (backoff not aggressive) -> retry amplification (retrywave) -> queue saturation -> 504s.

Evidence attached: kv-cache-traces-20270714.log (sampled traces showing eviction-then-miss loops), and a short scrub of leader-election logs.

Immediate mitigations applied at 11:52 PST:
- reverted the adaptive batching tweak on the west/us pool (rolled back to previous policy)
- temporarily disabled prefix cache for Acme's tenant id (route-specific flag)
- added a short token-threshold limiter to reduce oversized batch formation
- pushed a soft rate-limit on client retries via client-side header (recommended) — coordination with Acme underway

Current impact after mitigations: error rate down ~78% vs peak; P95 latency reduced to ~450ms (was >3s). We'll keep the rollback for 24 hours while we stabilize and run a controlled A/B to validate fixes.

Next steps (24 hours):
- deeper postmortem: root cause includes a bug in batch sizing logic + suboptimal eviction weights in prefix cache (INF-8893).
- code patch to batching heuristics and a cache weight tweak; QA + canary tomorrow morning.
- formal exec brief draft for Acme and internal stakeholders (I'll attach to the drive link).

Attachments: kv-cache-traces-20270714.log (log, 2.1 MB)
